pages.title: The Five Great Prophets
pages.content: Allah chose five leader prophets. They have a special title: The Five Great Messengers (In Arabic, this title is Ulul-Azm). The title means they were very patient and had a strong character. They had an important mission from Allah to guide people to Allah’s true path. They invited them to do good and stay away from bad. Allah asked them to be patient in their duty and trust His promise that He will save the believers. Those major prophets in Islam are Prophet Noah (pbuh), Prophet Abraham (pbuh), Prophet Moses (pbuh), Prophet Jesus (pbuh) and Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).

vocabulary.definition: Able to wait calmly without getting angry.
An important job someone is given.

pages.title: How Idol Worship Began
pages.content:
Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said: “The period between Adam and Noah was ten centuries.” (Ibn Abbas reported this.) During this long time between Prophet Adam (pbuh) and Prophet Noah (pbuh) many people lived. They remembered prophets’ words and worshipped only one Allah in the right way. As years passed, people forgot Allah’s messages. But there were some good men among Prophet Adam’s children. Their names were Wad, Suwa’, Yaghus, Ya’uk, and Nasr. They still prayed to Allah day and night. They loved Allah, so Allah loved them too. They told people to keep Allah’s messages in their minds. People also loved those good men and spoke about them with respect for a long time after they died.

People always missed these good men very much. To show respect, they first made pictures of them. Later, they also decided to make their stone statues. They put these statues in their houses and gave them the names of those good men.

At first, people did not pray to the statues. But then, everyone forgot the history of these old stone figures and started to worship them. They bowed down in front of the statues and prayed to them for good things.

After some time, Allah chose Noah (pbuh) as His messenger to give people good advice and tell them to stop worshipping statues.

vocabulary.definition: Told what someone said or did.
Shapes of people made of stone or wood.
Bent the body low to show respect.

pages.title: A Message for Everyone
pages.content:
Prophet Noah (pbuh) worked as a carpenter, according to Islamic reports. But he was a brave and smart man. He was also kind, honest and patient. He always told the truth. Allah said to him: “Warn your people before a big punishment comes.” So, Prophet Noah (pbuh) spoke to them and said again and again: “I am a true Messenger of Allah and I call you to believe in the One and Only Allah and to worship Him.”

When they heard the message, they chose two different paths. The poor and weak people believed Noah’s words. They believed him because Allah’s message says that believers are equal. There is no difference between the poor and the rich.

But the rich and powerful leaders were proud and did not listen to Noah (pbuh). They did not accept his message and told him, ‘We think you are totally wrong.’ They said this because they only wanted to protect their power. They never wanted to be near poor and weak people.

They began to argue with him. They said, “Could Allah not find anyone but you? Why did Allah choose you? You are just an ordinary person like us. You are not special, and you are not better than us. We think you are a liar! If Allah wanted, He could send angels instead.” Noah (pbuh) agreed and said he was only a human. Actually, a messenger needs to be a normal person, not an angel, so that people can understand him easily.

The rich men saw only poor and weak people around Noah (pbuh). Then, they decided to make a deal with him. They said poor people and rich people could not share the same belief. They asked Noah (pbuh) to keep the poor and weak people away from him. But Noah (pbuh) said, “I will never send away poor and weak believers.” He explained, “These people believe in Allah, so I will not send them away.”

The rich leaders said that their fathers and grandfathers prayed to idols. However, Noah (pbuh) knew the truth. Prophet Adam and Prophet Idris never prayed to idols. They only respected and loved Allah.

vocabulary.definition: Something bad that happens to someone because they did wrong.
A person who brings a message from Allah.
Speak angrily to someone because you do not agree.

pages.title: Nine Hundred and Fifty Years
pages.content:
Prophet Noah (pbuh) kept talking to his people and continued to invite them to Allah: “My people, follow my message from Allah. There is no other god but Allah. I worry about your punishment on a bad day.” The group of leaders said, “We see that you are making a big mistake.” Noah (pbuh) replied, “My people, I am making no mistake. I am a messenger from the Lord of the Universe. I bring you the words of Allah and give you helpful advice.” Noah (pbuh) also explained that it is not right to pray to a piece of stone or wood. This belief makes people accept everything without thinking and does not let them think in the right way.

Prophet Noah (pbuh) never gave up on his mission. He tried to help his people see the truth. He did not want anything for himself. Instead, he continued to warn them with a sad but honest heart.

The argument between Noah (pbuh) and his people did not end. Noah (pbuh) kept telling them Allah’s message. He continued to teach his people for 950 years. But when he started to talk about Allah’s message, they covered their ears, hid their heads under their clothes, and they did not change their mind. At first, they laughed at Noah and made fun of his words. Then, they became very cruel to him. In the end, they beat him so badly that he almost died, but Noah (pbuh) stayed strong.

Noah (pbuh) was still patient and kind. Then, Allah told him that no more people would believe him. After that, Noah (pbuh) knew these people would never change, and he prayed, ‘My Lord! Please do not leave any cruel people on earth. If they stay, they will stop others from following You. They will teach their children to be against You.’ In the end, Allah accepted Noah’s prayer.

vocabulary.definition: Have a new idea or opinion.
Laughed to make someone look silly.
Said unkind things to laugh at someone.

pages.title: The Ark
pages.content:
Allah told Noah (pbuh) to build an ark, a very large boat. Allah said a huge flood was coming to punish the cruel people because they did not listen to Him.

Allah showed Noah (pbuh) where to build the ship. He started to build this large boat outside the city with wood and nails. It was far away from the sea. Noah (pbuh) followed Allah’s plan with great faith and trust.

People laughed and talked about the ship on the land, far from any water. They did not believe the great power of Allah, so they could not understand why Noah (pbuh) built a ship so far from the water. They called him crazy. But soon, they were going to see Allah’s great miracle. The Ark began to look ready. When it was finished, Noah (pbuh) waited quietly for Allah’s message.

And finally, the time came. When water started to pour from the sky and come up from the ground, Allah told Noah (pbuh) to go into the ark with the believers and his family, except those who did not believe. Allah also told him to take two of every animal and insect. Unbelievers looked at him and asked, “What are you doing with all those animals?”

The believers got on the ark. Some reports say there were about 80 people on it. But Noah’s wife and son did not believe his words, so they did not join them.

The people and animals went inside. The Ark kept the believers safe from the heavy rain and the water coming from the ground. Suddenly, the ground under the sea moved and the water pushed up. Giant waves flooded the land. They lifted the Ark and made it look very small, like a toy ship in the sea. This wooden boat became a safe home because the people in it believed in Allah with all their hearts.

Noah (pbuh) was safe inside his big ship too. Then, he saw his son not far from the ship. He shouted, “Come inside and stay safe!” But his son did not listen and said, “I will run up a mountain. I will be safe from the water there.” Noah (pbuh) said, “Only Allah can save you today.” Then a wave came between them, and his son drowned.

vocabulary.definition: Small, thin pieces of metal that join pieces of wood.
People who do not believe in Allah.

pages.title: The Flood Ends
pages.content:
Allah said: “Earth, take the water back! Sky, stop the rain!” Then, the water went down and Allah’s plan was completed. The ship landed safely on Mount Judi. The water went away.

Noah (pbuh) let the animals, birds, and insects go, and they went to live all over the earth. Noah (pbuh) and the believers left the ark. He put his head on the ground to thank Allah.

pages.title: Noah’s Last Advice
pages.content:
Years passed. Now Noah (pbuh) was very old. Before he died, he called his children and gave them some important advice. First, he told them to believe only in Allah and never to pray to other gods. He said, “To believe in Allah is more important than everything in the world.” Second, he told them never to be arrogant.

Most of Noah’s people did not listen to his warning long ago. But Muslims still remember his story and advice today.

vocabulary.definition: Thinking that you are better than other people.

vocabulary.definition: An important job someone is given.
vocabulary.storyExample: They had an important mission from Allah to guide people to Allah’s true path.
They had an important mission from Allah to guide people to Allah’s true path.
They invited them to do good and stay away from bad.
Those major prophets in Islam are Prophet Noah (pbuh), Prophet Abraham (pbuh), Prophet Moses (pbuh), Prophet Jesus (pbuh) and Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).

vocabulary.definition: Told what someone said or did.
vocabulary.storyExample: (Ibn Abbas reported this.) During this long time between Prophet Adam (pbuh) and Prophet Noah (pbuh) many people lived.
They told people to keep Allah’s messages in their minds.
To show respect, they first made pictures of them.

vocabulary.definition: Shapes of people made of stone or wood.
vocabulary.storyExample: But then, everyone forgot the history of these old stone figures and started to worship them.

vocabulary.definition: Bent the body low to show respect.

They still prayed to Allah day and night.
But he was a brave and smart man.
But he was a brave and smart man.

vocabulary.definition: Something bad that happens to someone because they did wrong.
vocabulary.storyExample: Allah said to him: “Warn your people before a big punishment comes.”

vocabulary.definition: A person who brings a message from Allah.
vocabulary.storyExample: So, Prophet Noah (pbuh) spoke to them and said again and again: “I am a true Messenger of Allah and I call you to believe in the One and Only Allah and to worship Him.”
When they heard the message, they chose two different paths.

vocabulary.storyExample: Then, they decided to make a deal with him.

But Noah (pbuh) said, “I will never send away poor and weak believers.”

vocabulary.definition: Had a very good opinion of.

Prophet Noah (pbuh) never gave up on his mission.

vocabulary.definition: Have a new idea or opinion.
vocabulary.storyExample: But when he started to talk about Allah’s message, they covered their ears, hid their heads under their clothes, and they did not change their mind.

vocabulary.definition: Laughed to make someone look silly.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review and use the language of the whole book.

exercises.title: Look: Before or After the Flood?
exercises.instructions: Sort the events into two groups.
exercises.question: Did it happen before or after the flood?

items: Noah taught his people for 950 years.
The ship landed on Mount Judi.

Before the flood: Noah taught his people for 950 years.
After the flood: The ship landed on Mount Judi.

exercises.explanation: Chapters 2–5 tell what happened before the flood; Chapter 6 tells what happened after it.

feedback.incorrect: Was the water still there?

exercises.title: Look: Past Forms
exercises.instructions: Choose the sentence with a correct past form.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Noah built the ark far from the sea.
Noah builded the ark far from the sea.
Noah build the ark far from the sea.
exercises.explanation: “Build” is an irregular verb. Its past form is “built”.

feedback.incorrect: What is the past of build?

exercises.title: Look: Kept + -ing
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: In “Noah kept talking to his people”, kept talking means he talked again and again.
exercises.explanation: “Keep + -ing” means to do something again and again.

feedback.incorrect: Did he stop?

exercises.title: Practise: Linking Words
exercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
exercises.question: Which word fits?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The poor people believed Noah [blank] believers are equal. A messenger is a normal person [blank] people can understand him. The ship was far from the sea, [blank] people laughed.
exercises.explanation: “Because” gives a reason. “So that” gives a purpose. “So” gives a result.

feedback.correct: Well done. Because, so that, so.
feedback.incorrect: Is it a reason, a purpose or a result?

exercises.title: Practise: Choose the Form
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence.
exercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: He continued [choice] his people for 950 years.
Noah let the animals [choice].
He told them never [choice] arrogant.

exercises.explanation: Use “continue to + verb”, “let + base verb” and “tell someone never to + verb”.

feedback.correct: Correct. To teach, go, to be.
feedback.incorrect: Check the verb patterns.

exercises.title: Practise: Correct the Sentences
exercises.instructions: Find the mistake and choose the correct form.
exercises.question: Which form is correct?

errorItems.sentence: Noah kept tell them Allah’s message.
The Ark kept the believers safe of the rain.

exercises.explanation: Use “were” with plural subjects, “kept + -ing” and “safe from”.

feedback.incorrect: Check the verb forms and the preposition.

exercises.title: Use: A New Context
exercises.instructions: Read about a sports team. Fill each gap from the word bank.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s words in a new text?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Our football coach is very [blank]. Our [blank] is to win the school cup. We lost many games, but we never [blank]. The coach says a good player is never [blank].
exercises.explanation: Patient, mission, gave up and arrogant come from the book. Here they describe a sports team.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s words in a new text.
feedback.incorrect: Read the words around each gap.

exercises.title: Use: Check a Short Text
exercises.instructions: A student wrote about a rainy day. Find each mistake.
exercises.question: What should the student change?

errorItems.sentence: We stayed inside for keep dry.
My mother told us to not go out.

exercises.explanation: Use the past simple with yesterday, “to + verb” for purpose, and “told someone not to + verb”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Rained, to keep, not to go.
feedback.incorrect: Check the verb forms.

exercises.title: Use: A Lesson from Noah
exercises.instructions: Write four to five sentences about one lesson from Noah’s story.
exercises.question: Which lesson is the most important for you?
exercises.explanation: Example: “One lesson from Noah’s story is patience. For example, Noah taught his people for 950 years and never gave up. Sometimes I want to stop when my homework is difficult. I can try again because patience helps me learn.”

feedback.correct: Check: the lesson, an example and because.

discussionPrompts.question: Say the lesson.
discussionPrompts.example: One lesson from Noah’s story is …

discussionPrompts.question: Give an example from the book.
Say how you can follow it, with because.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole book together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: The Mission
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer from the book.
exercises.question: What was the mission of the great messengers?
options: to guide people to Allah’s true path
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “They had an important mission from Allah to guide people to Allah’s true path.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the beginning of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Words and Meanings
exercises.instructions: Match each word with its meaning.
exercises.question: What do the words mean?

matchingPairs.right: small pieces of metal for wood
thinking you are better than others

correctAnswer.nails: small pieces of metal for wood
correctAnswer.arrogant: thinking you are better than others

exercises.explanation: These words appear in Chapters 1, 5 and 7.

feedback.correct: Correct. Each word matches its meaning.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the Word Notes.

exercises.title: Ten Centuries
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 2 with one word.
exercises.question: How long was the period between Adam and Noah?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The period between Adam and Noah was ten [blank].
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “The period between Adam and Noah was ten centuries.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first sentence of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Why They Believed
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer from the book.
exercises.question: Why did the poor and weak people believe Noah?
options: Allah’s message says that believers are equal.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “They believed him because Allah’s message says that believers are equal.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Who Did What?
exercises.instructions: Match each person or group with what they did.
exercises.question: Who did what?

matchingPairs.right: built the ark far from the sea
asked Noah to send away the poor
wanted to run up a mountain

correctAnswer.Noah: built the ark far from the sea
correctAnswer.the rich leaders: asked Noah to send away the poor
correctAnswer.Noah’s son: wanted to run up a mountain

exercises.explanation: These people appear in Chapters 3 and 5.

feedback.incorrect: Look in Chapters 3 and 5.

exercises.title: Noah’s Character
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: Noah was brave, kind, honest and patient.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “But he was a brave and smart man. He was also kind, honest and patient.”

feedback.correct: Correct. He was all of these.
feedback.incorrect: Read the beginning of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: The Animals
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: Allah told Noah to take ten of every animal.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “Allah also told him to take two of every animal and insect.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the fourth paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: The Landing
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 6 with one word.
exercises.question: Where did the ship land?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The ship landed safely on Mount [blank].
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “The ship landed safely on Mount Judi.”

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 6.

exercises.title: Last Advice
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer from the book.
exercises.question: What did Noah say is more important than everything in the world?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “To believe in Allah is more important than everything in the world.”

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 7.

exercises.title: Noah’s Story
exercises.instructions: Put the events in order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: Allah chose Noah as His messenger.
Noah taught his people for 950 years.
The ship landed on Mount Judi.
Noah gave his children his last advice.

exercises.explanation: The book tells Noah’s story from his mission to his last advice.

feedback.correct: Correct. From his mission to his last advice.
feedback.incorrect: Follow the chapters in order.
